sentences.text: I have heard the submissions of Sh.Lavkesh Anand, ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Sh.Indrajeet & Sh.Ved Tripathi, ld. Counsels for respondent no.2/insurance company.
I have also gone through the written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner and respondent no.2.

My issue wise finding is as follows :
Issue No.1 8.

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of accident having occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
As such, petitioner has to establish occurring of an accident and that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others.

It is in that factual context insurance company/respondent no.2 has taken the plea that delay in registration of the FIR and the manner in which eye witness Abdul Kuddus and Siraj Khan were introduced, certainly create doubt about the concoction and false implication of vehicle/truck no. UP-15AT-3608 only for obtaining the compensation from insurance company.
It is also the submission of counsels for insurance that beside delay in registration of FIR and introduction of eye witness, only eye witness examined is PW3 Abdul Kuddus.

It is submitted that cross examination of PW3 would also shows that evidence of that witness is most contradictory and unworthy of reliance for proving the involvement as well as rash and negligent driving of driver of vehicle no. UP-15AT- 3608.

It is argued that admittedly deceased in the present case died when the Alto car no.UP-15AP-8935 which deceased was driving,
dashed into a tree nearby the road.
It is submitted that in such circumstances it is quite possible that insured vehicle no.UP-15AT-3608 stated to be offending vehicle was not involved in the accident at all.

10. Counsel for the petitioner on the other hand submitted that this Tribunal need to decide the issue regarding involvement as well as rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle no.UP-15AT-3608, by preponderance of probabilities based on the evidence as come on the record.

It is submitted by counsel for the petitioner that due to continuous efforts made by petitioner Mehak Singh, he could contact with eye witness Abdul Kuddus and Siraj Khan and it is on the efforts made by the petitioner, the case could work out and thereupon police took the action.
As such it is argued that it is not that every case wherein there has been delay in registration of FIR, same would be viewed with suspicion of false implication.
11. Keeping in view rival submissions made at bar, let us first examine the evidence.

PW1 Mehak Singh admittedly is not eye witness to the accident, therefore for deciding the issue under consideration, let us straightaway examine the evidence of PW3 Abdul Kuddus, an eye witness who stated that on 14.03.2016 he was going from Meerut side to Behrot on his motorcycle and when he reached neat petrol pump Rohta, a truck no. UP-15AT-3608 came from Khivai side i.e. opposite side in a rash and negligent manner.

In the meantime a "Neel Gay" suddenly came on the road and in order to escape the truck from collusion with that "Neel Gay", driver of the truck no.UP-15AT-3608 lost balance and hit the Alto car no.UP-15AP-8935.
PW3 further says that on account of such collusion of truck with the car, the car dashed into a tree by the side of the road, resultantly the driver of the car (deceased), died at the spot.

12. PW3 however gave certain unnatural responses in cross examination when he stated that he does not remember the date of accident; he did not accompany the deceased to hospital, after the accident; he did not call the police; he though recorded registration number of the offending vehicle but he gave his own mobile number to a passerby and later got a MACT No.2411/16 Presha Chaudhary & Ors. vs. Asif and Ors.

sentences.text: Page 6 call from PS Rohta after about one and a half month of the accident.
PW3 also stated in his cross examination that police never recorded his statement.
It is due to such responses of PW3 in cross examination, counsel for the insurance company submits that his evidence is worthy of no reliance.

13. Having considered the evidence of PW3 in entirety, it be noted that though there are certain unnatural/unbelievable responses from witness PW3 but examining his testimony as a whole gives an impression that he actually saw the accident but behaved in an unresponsive manner, by leaving the place of accident without taking the injured/deceased in the accident to hospital or to inform to the police authorities.
Such conduct though is not responsible one but given the overall standard of the society many people do behave in that manner.
People do saw the accident, injured in the accident but do not come forward to help or to inform to the police.
Therefore such conduct though is not responsible or like a law abiding citizen but very much existing in the society.
Thus, because of such conduct evidence of the witness cannot be thrown away as a whole.
More particularly in a case for claim in an accident.
Admittedly in the present case a human life has lost in an accident.
That being not disputed, now question is regarding involvement and rash and negligent driving of vehicle no.UP-15AT-3608.
PW3 stated that he was following car of the deceased when accident occurred.
PW3 further stated that he was at the distance of 100 feet behind the car of the deceased.
PW3 further stated that truck driver did not stop the truck even for a minute after the accident and fled away from there.
PW3 further stated that he noted down registration number of the offending vehicle.

Police papers/police diary indicate that PW3 along with one Siraj Khan while one day while taking tea stated regarding seeing of the accident and their conversation having been heard by PW1, thereupon local police contacted the witness and case stated to have worked out showing involvement of offending vehicle.

Important to note here is that on the basis of statements of PW3 as well as Siraj Khan local police has charge sheeted respondent no.1 as an accused in FIR No.92/2016 regarding the accident in question.

Moreover if we examine the police papers which include certified copy of site plan, even as per police version also accident occurred when driver of the truck no.UP- 15AT-3608 tried to escape from sudden crossing over of Neel Gay on the main road, lost the control of the vehicle and dashed into Alto car of the deceased and due to the impact of the accident Alto car of the deceased hit with a tree by the side of the road.

As such site plan also corroborate the deposition of PW3.
15.

No doubt there has been delay in the FIR but it is not that in every case whenever there is a delay, Tribunal should assume manipulation or false implication of offending vehicle only for making out a false claim of compensation.
There must be some material on the record beside delay in FIR, for giving judicial satisfaction to the Tribunal regarding concoction and false implication of the vehicle for claim.
In the absence of same, delay in lodging of FIR itself cannot be a reason to disbelieve the version of the petitioner.
This Tribunal has already examined the evidence of PW3 as well as other material on the record.

Therefore this Tribunal is of considered view that involvement of offending vehicle no.UP-15AT-3608 and causing of accident by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 is MACT No.2411/16 Presha Chaudhary & Ors. vs. Asif and Ors.

As such this issue stands decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 16.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 17.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Sangeeta Tomar.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: If these determinations are standardized
, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.

"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As per the claim petition, deceased Smt. Sangeeta Tomar died in a roadside accident on 14.03.2016, at about 08:30 a.m., when she was driving her Alto Car bearing registration no. UP- 15AP-8935 and she was proceeding towards her school, when she reached near petrol pump, Rohta, Distt. Meerut, U.P., a truck bearing registration Km. Presha Chaudhary vs Asif And Ors on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20183269/
1 no.UP-15AT-3608 came from opposite side in rash and negligent manner and suddenly a Neel Gay appeared/crossed over on road and in the process of escaping, the truck driver could not control over his vehicle no.UP- 15AT-3608 and hit the car of deceased from its side.
Presha Chaudhary & Ors. vs. Asif and Ors.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of pleadings as come on the record, Ld. Predecessor of this court on 23.10.2017 framed following issues:
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.
UP-15AT-3608 on 14.03.2016 at about 08:30 am near Petrol Pump, Rohta, District Meerut, U.P. in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hti against the car bearing registration no.
UP-15AP-8935 being driven by Sangeeta Tomar and thereafter Car dashed against roadside tree as a result Sangeeta Tomar sustained fatal injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of accident having occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
As such, petitioner has to establish occurring of an accident and that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
Such conduct though is not responsible one but given the overall standard of the society many people do behave in that manner.
People do saw the accident, injured in the accident but do not come forward to help or to inform to the police.
Therefore such conduct though is not responsible or like a law abiding citizen but very much existing in the society.
Thus, because of such conduct evidence of the witness cannot be thrown away as a whole.
More particularly in a case for claim in an accident.
Admittedly in the present case a human life has lost in an accident.
Moreover if we examine the police papers which include certified copy of site plan, even as per police version also accident occurred when driver of the truck no.UP- 15AT-3608 tried to escape from sudden crossing over of Neel Gay on the main road, lost the control of the vehicle and dashed into Alto car of the deceased and due to the impact of the accident Alto car of the deceased hit with a tree by the side of the road.
As such site plan also corroborate the deposition of PW3.
15.
No doubt there has been delay in the FIR but it is not that in every case whenever there is a delay, Tribunal should assume manipulation or false implication of offending vehicle only for making out a false claim of compensation.
There must be some material on the record beside delay in FIR, for giving judicial satisfaction to the Tribunal regarding concoction and false implication of the vehicle for claim.
In the absence of same, delay in lodging of FIR itself cannot be a reason to disbelieve the version of the petitioner.
Therefore this Tribunal is of considered view that involvement of offending vehicle no.UP-15AT-3608 and causing of accident by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 is MACT No.2411/16 Presha Chaudhary & Ors. vs. Asif and Ors.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Having considered the evidence and taking note of salary slip Ex.PW1/4 as well as document Ex.PW2/A, it is established that gross pay of the deceased while she was working as a Government Teacher was Rs.41,610/- per month and there was a deduction of income tax of Rs.5,748/- per month.
25. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 39 MACT No.2411/16
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is submitted that in such circumstances it is quite possible that insured vehicle no.UP-15AT-3608 stated to be offending vehicle was not involved in the accident at all.

Instant claim petition has been filed by four petitioners i.e. minor children and parents of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by four dependents, one-fourth of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards her personal living expenses.
In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-

(a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant i.e., the savings bank account of the claimant shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
(b) The original fixed deposit shall be retained by the bank in safe custody.
(c) The monthly interest be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the claimant near the place of their residence.
(d) The maturity amounts of the FDR be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the claimant near the place of their residence.
(e) No loan, advance, withdrawal or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the fixed deposits without permission of the Court.
(f) The concerned bank shall not issue any cheque book and/or debit card to claimant.
However, in case the debit card and/or cheque book have already been issued, bank shall cancel the same before the disbursement of the award amount.
The bank shall debit card(s) freeze MACT No.2411/16 Presha Chaudhary & Ors. vs. Asif and Ors. Page 17 the account of the claimant
so that no debit card be issued in respect of the account of the claimant from any other branch of the bank.

(g) The bank shall make an endorsement on the passbook of the claimant to the effect that no cheque book and/or debit card have been issued and shall not be issued without the permission of the Court and claimant shall produce the passbook with the necessary endorsement before the Court on the next date fixed for compliance.
